more_info.overview: Adipic acid is an organic dicarboxylic acid used for acidity control in specified foods. Its acidity-regulating role is to adjust or maintain the pH of the food. The specified material is supplied as white powder or crystalline material. Only a limited amount dissolves in water, according to the specification.
more_info.daily_intake: For adipic acid: 0-5 mg/kg body weight (JECFA, 2025). This evaluation does not establish an ADI for every form in the named group. This is the combined limit for adipic acid and its specified salts.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; desserts excluding products covered in categories 1, 3 and 4.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
